section_summary: This section covers diplomatic and interagency actions regarding the revision of Japan's National Public Service Law between September 1948 and September 1949. It details U.S. debates involving the State, Army, and Labor Departments and the Civil Service Commission over civil servants' rights to strike and negotiate, alongside efforts in the Far Eastern Commission to counter Soviet and British criticisms. It also analyzes the Japanese political aftermath, including Diet passage of the bill under the Yoshida Cabinet, widespread union job desertions and arrests, leftist party realignment, and National Personnel Authority regulations banning civil servants from political activities.

subfiles.about: Statement setting forth the U.S. position rejecting a Soviet proposal on Japanese government workers' rights in the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.from: United States Representative to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Rejects the Soviet draft policy on Japanese public servants, defending MacArthur's strike prevention actions as necessary and legal.
subfiles.title: Statement of United States Position on Policy Decision Proposed by the Soviet Representative

subfiles.about: Transmittal memorandum enclosing the U.S. policy statement opposing the Soviet draft resolution on Japanese public workers.
subfiles.from: C. E. Saltzman (Assistant Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Recommends limiting Commission debate and bringing the Soviet proposal to an early vote, transmitting the U.S. position statement.
subfiles.title: Memorandum to the United States Member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Draft text for the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission countering Soviet allegations regarding Japanese labor policy.
subfiles.summary: Argues the Soviet proposal is based on factual errors, denies MacArthur acted extralegally, and justifies temporary restrictions on public employee strikes.
subfiles.title: Draft Statement of United States Position on Policy Decision Proposed by the Soviet Representative
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission

subfiles.about: Routing slip asking Butterworth to draft an acknowledgment to Frances Perkins's letter for Under Secretary Lovett.
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett (Under Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Requests a draft acknowledgment to Frances Perkins's letter on Japanese civil service policy.
subfiles.title: Note to Mr. Butterworth Regarding Frances Perkins Letter

subfiles.about: Letter questioning the extension of collective bargaining rights to Japanese civil service and public corporation employees.
subfiles.summary: Objects to collective bargaining provisions for Japanese public servants as contrary to U.S. civil service principles.
subfiles.title: Letter from Frances Perkins to Robert A. Lovett
subfiles.to: Robert A. Lovett (Under Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Memorandum reviewing the Japanese civil service dispute and submitting a recommended policy cable to MacArthur.
subfiles.summary: Reviews the controversy over public workers' rights, notes SCAP's lack of prior consultation with State and Sebald, and recommends policy guidance.
subfiles.title: Japanese Government Workers' Rights
subfiles.to: Robert A. Lovett (Under Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Draft State Department cable offering guidance and recommendations on proposed Japanese public service legislation.
subfiles.summary: Recommends SCAP base strike bans on occupation necessity to comply with FEC policy. Urges non-strike bargaining and arbitration rights for industrial employees, clarifies representation rights, and reviews penal and rule-making powers.
subfiles.title: Department of State Draft Cable to SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: Routing slip regarding the urgency of cable clearance before distribution of the Army version.
subfiles.summary: Urges action on the cable draft before the Army version is distributed.
subfiles.title: Department of State Reference Slip

subfiles.about: Final interagency-approved cable instructing General MacArthur on Japanese civil service and public corporation laws.
subfiles.from: Department of State and Department of the Army
subfiles.summary: Conveys final U.S. policy guidance on proposed public service legislation, including an addition by Secretary Royall. Advises providing negotiation and arbitration mechanisms for government industrial workers to maintain Allied support in the FEC and UN.
subfiles.title: Final Approved Draft Cable to SCAP Tokyo

subfiles.about: Letter responding to Frances Perkins and explaining why the State Department supports limited negotiation rights for Japanese industrial workers.
subfiles.from: Robert A. Lovett (Acting Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Explains to Perkins that international relations and occupation policy justify non-coercive collective bargaining for government industrial employees.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of State to Frances Perkins

subfiles.about: Official record copy of the memorandum detailing background on Japanese civil service legislation and transmitting the draft cable.
subfiles.summary: Official record copy of memorandum reviewing Japanese civil service controversy and proposing draft cable to SCAP.
subfiles.title: Japanese Government Workers' Rights (Record Copy)
subfiles.to: Robert A. Lovett (Under Secretary of State)

subfiles.about: Letter presenting the Labor Department's stance on union representation and collective bargaining for Japanese communication workers.
subfiles.from: John W. Gibson (Acting Secretary of Labor)
subfiles.summary: Urges precise instructions ensuring public employees may join lawful unions and giving communication workers bargaining rights similar to railway employees.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of Labor to Secretary of the Army
subfiles.to: Kenneth C. Royall (Secretary of the Army)

subfiles.about: Outgoing telegram requesting urgent airmail delivery of the Japanese Government's draft revision of the Public Service Law.
subfiles.summary: Requests urgent airmailing of two official English copies of the latest draft revision of the National Public Service Law.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram to SCAP Tokyo for Acting Political Adviser

subfiles.about: Central records form designating a replacement record copy for Tokyo Despatch 702.
subfiles.summary: Designates attached copy of Despatch 702 as the permanent central record copy.
subfiles.title: Central Records Replacement Sheet for Despatch 702

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on Cabinet deliberations on the Public Service Law, union job desertions, and police arrests.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald (U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Reports on revisions to the negotiation clause and encloses police statistics on arrests of railway and communications workers for job desertions.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 702: Developments in Connection with the National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording British representations regarding the omission of independent arbitration machinery in the draft law.
subfiles.summary: Records discussion with British representative Graves, who delivered a statement urging independent arbitration machinery for Japanese civil servants under Article 98.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: UK Position on National Public Service Law Before Japanese Diet

subfiles.about: Routing notice indicating that enclosures listed for Despatch 774 were not received with the despatch.
subfiles.summary: Notes that enclosures purportedly accompanying the despatch were missing and would be routed when received.
subfiles.title: Division of Communications and Records Routing Slip

subfiles.about: Comprehensive political report on the Japanese Diet's passage of the National Public Service Law and its repercussions on political parties and labor.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald (U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Analyzes political fallout from the passage of the revised Public Service Law on November 30, 1948, and MacArthur's statement. Examines Socialist defection, Communist opposition and labor leadership under Dobashi, and the strengthening of conservative forces under Yoshida.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 774: Political Repercussions of Revision of National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Airgram reporting on National Personnel Authority Rule 14-7 restricting political activities of civil servants.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes National Personnel Authority Rule 14-7 banning civil servants from seventeen categories of political activities, quoting Authority President Asai on civil service neutrality.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-215: National Personnel Authority Ruling on Political Activities of Civil Servants
